newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: BP says rebels threaten Colombian projects.
newsitem.headline: BP says rebels threaten Colombian projects.

text.p: The chief of British Petroleum Co Plc has warned that mounting leftist guerrilla activity in Colombia could force it to abandon some of its oil exploration projects in the country, a top government official said Tuesday.

Energy and Mines Minister Rodrigo Villamizar said the warning from BP director general John Browne was made Monday evening when he met President Ernesto Samper at the Casa de Narino presidential palace.

"If security isn't reinforced, especially in exploration areas, he told us that it's possible they (BP) will have to lower the level of explorations and even abandon some projects," Villamizar told reporters.

He added that BP, the single largest foreign investor in Colombia, had specifically conditioned any further exploration activity in the promising Piedemonte block in Colombia's eastern plains to a beefed up military presence in the area.

Military officials have complained in the past that roughly 35 percent of their thinly-stretched 100,000-strong combat force is devoted full-time to guarding infrastructure and oil and coal facilities across Colombia.
Guerrillas, meanwhile, have stepped up their military activity throughout the country over the past year.

Villamizar, who sat in on the talks between Browne and Samper, said the president had ordered an extraordinary meeting of Colombia's national security council to study the problems faced by BP and other multinational oil giants and look at ways of addressing them.
"Our concern is that this could have an add-on effect on other companies," Villamizar said.

In a related development, police said Tuesday that a U.S. geologist working on a gold mining project in southwest Colombia was kidnapped by Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia (FARC) rebels earlier this month.

The kidnapping followed that of another U.S. geologist by unidentified gunmen in December. In early February, suspected Marxist guerrillas also abducted a Houston oilman in Venezuela and are believed to have brought him across the border to Colombia.
